Article Title: ‘Protocol, not power’: Ex-IMF director rebuts Pakistan’s 'historic milestone' claim over 2027 leadership
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Former International Monetary Fund (IMF) executive director Krishnamurthy V Subramanian has challenged Pakistan’s claim that its appointment to chair the IMF and World Bank Boards of Governors in 2027 marks a return to global financial leadership, calling the role “protocol, not power”.In a post on X, Subramanian said the chairmanship was ceremonial and rotated annually, arguing that it should not be equated with leadership of a major global economic forum.“Claim: ‘Pakistan is heading back to the top table of global finance after 74 years!’ Reality: Pakistan will chair the IMF-World Bank Annual Plenary in 2027. This chair is purely ceremonial & rotates annually: Paraguay this year, Cabo Verde in 2025. It's protocol, not power,” he wrote.Pakistan was recently named chair of the Boards of Governors of the IMF and the World Bank Group for 2027. The country will take up the position for the first time since 1953, with Pakistan’s Minister for Economic Affairs and World Bank governor, Ahad Khan Cheema, set to assume the role, according to an Islamabad statement.Pakistan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs described the appointment as a “historic milestone”, saying it would give the country an opportunity to contribute to global economic and development discussions and facilitate dialogue among member nations.In another post, Subramanian rejected comparisons between India’s presidencies of the G20 and BRICS and Pakistan’s rotating chairmanship of the IMF-World Bank Annual Plenary, calling them a false equivalence.“India's G20 presidency set the agenda for a major forum of global economic cooperation; its BRICS presidency drove an emerging-economies platform... Pakistan's role is to preside over an annual meeting,” he said.Pakistan continues to rely on financial assistance from the IMF through a $7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and a $1.4 billion Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).The EFF is intended to address the country’s balance-of-payments needs and support economic reforms, while the RSF provides longer-term financing to help tackle climate-related risks and strengthen economic resilience.Pakistan is also expected to receive around $1.2 billion from the IMF, subject to approval by the fund’s Executive Board. The expected disbursement follows an agreement between IMF staff and Pakistani authorities on the latest reviews of the two loan programmes.
Article Summary: Pakistan was recently named chair of the Boards of Governors of the IMF and the World Bank Group for 2027. The country will take up the position for the first time since 1953. Pakistan continues to rely on financial assistance from the IMF through a $7 billion Extended Fund Facility.

Article Title: Menopause is normal, suffering through it shouldn't be
Article Text:
Is menopause in women treatable?

Indian Journal of Preventive & Social Medicine

Menopause can bring a range of physical, emotional and urogenital symptoms, affecting women’s sleep, mood and everyday lives.

When menopause symptoms are dismissed as ‘just ageing’

Treatment options for menopause range from hormone therapy and non-hormonal medicines to lifestyle changes

The doctor’s dilemma: recognising symptoms, choosing treatment

Is India’s healthcare system prepared for menopause?

Treatments available in India

How social stigma plays a role

Dr Soy talks to TOI

She lies awake at night. The next morning, she struggles to concentrate at work, snaps at loved ones over things that never bothered her before, or wonders why her own body suddenly feels unfamiliar.For some women, menopause arrives quietly; for others, it brings a wave of physical and emotional changes that can leave them exhausted, anxious and searching for answers.And often, the hardest part is not just dealing with the symptoms, but getting someone to take them seriously.Menopause is a natural biological transition, but the symptoms can be disruptive enough to affect everyday life. While some women dismiss them as stress or ageing, others find their concerns brushed aside or are unsure where to turn for help. Despite growing conversations around women's health, gaps in awareness, medical guidance and access to appropriate treatment continue to shape their experiences.A quantitative descriptive survey involving 150 women from urban areas assessed the impact of menopausal symptoms on quality of life. The study, published in the, was authored by Somibala Thokchom and David Ratna Paul Talagathoti.Participants aged 40 to 55 years completed the 11-item Menopause Rating Scale (MRS) to assess their symptoms and a modified 32-item Menopause-Specific Quality of Life Questionnaire (MENQOL) to evaluate how menopause affected their daily lives.The study found that 58.7% of participants were aged 40–45 years, while 75.3% had already experienced menopause. Overall, 92% reported moderate to severe symptoms, 4.7% experienced mild symptoms and 3.3% reported very severe symptoms. Nearly all participants (99.3%) reported changes in their daily routines.Although the findings cannot be generalised to all Indian women, given the small, urban sample, they highlight the potential impact of menopause on everyday life.The question is not simply how women experience menopause, but why so many may struggle to recognise their symptoms, seek medical advice or access appropriate care.Many women continue to experience menopause symptoms without seeking medical help, often assuming that fatigue, anxiety, disturbed sleep and mood changes are an inevitable part of ageing.Doctors say this can delay assessment and treatment, particularly when women prioritise family and work responsibilities over their own health.“Menopause is a natural condition, but that does not necessarily imply that symptoms cannot be treated,” said Dr Mitul Gupta, senior consultant, obstetrics and gynaecology, Cocoon Hospital, Jaipur.Dr Gupta cautioned against attributing symptoms to ageing without proper examination. Fatigue, irritability and poor concentration can also occur with conditions such as thyroid disorders, anaemia, sleep disorders and anxiety, making a detailed medical assessment important.Maya, a Uttar Pradesh native who now lives in Delhi, said, “I started experiencing menopause when I was 51. I did face difficulties, but back then, we didn’t really talk about these things at home. I used to feel hesitant."“I thought it was just a normal part of aging, and no one in my family really knew what I was going through. Even today, many families are unaware of what women experience during menopause, and often, women end up dealing with it on their own,” she adds.Menopause care extends beyond irregular periods and hot flashes. Hormonal changes can affect sleep, mood and sexual health, while the menopausal transition is also an important time to discuss longer-term health concerns, including bone health.A systematic review titledexamined 23 studies reporting symptoms among menopausal women in India. The review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and included eligibility criteria, a literature search, screening and data extraction.The review found that somatic symptoms were the most frequently reported category, with an average of 73.66% across the studies. Joint and muscular pain and fatigue were the most commonly reported complaints, followed by hot flashes.Psychological symptoms were reported in an average of 63.03% of women in the studies assessing this category. Eighteen studies reported psychosomatic symptoms, while five did not report psychological symptoms.Urogenital symptoms were reported in 13 studies, with an average prevalence of 51.40%. Ten studies did not report symptoms in this category. Although urogenital symptoms were the least frequently reported, the review noted that women who experienced them reported greater symptom intensity.The findings highlight the range of symptoms associated with menopause and the importance of recognising them rather than dismissing them as an unavoidable consequence of ageing. The percentages are averages reported across the reviewed studies and should not be interpreted as prevalence estimates for all Indian women.Menopause symptoms can vary considerably from one woman to another, making individual assessment essential before deciding on treatment.Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) can help women experiencing troublesome symptoms, including hot flashes and night sweats, but it is not suitable for everyone. Decisions about treatment must take into account an individual's symptoms, medical history, age, time since menopause and potential risks.“HRT is neither universally dangerous nor suitable for everyone. The right treatment is the one that is carefully chosen according to your individual needs, with proper medical guidance and regular follow-up,” said Dr Bharti Soy, consultant, obstetrics and gynaecology, Fortis O.P. Jindal Hospital & Research Centre.Doctors emphasise that consultations should cover the potential benefits and risks of hormone therapy, as well as non-hormonal alternatives where appropriate. Women should be able to discuss their concerns and make informed decisions with their healthcare providers.Symptoms should not automatically be attributed to menopause, as other medical conditions may require separate investigation and treatment. A thorough consultation can help distinguish between menopause-related changes and other possible causes, allowing care to be tailored to the individual's needs.Awareness alone may not be enough if women cannot access appropriate and affordable care. Gaps in menopause-specific knowledge, counselling and healthcare access can leave women without adequate guidance on managing their symptoms.The challenge is not limited to the availability of gynaecologists, but also whether consultations address menopause-related concerns beyond menstrual changes. Symptoms affecting sleep, mood, sexual wellbeing and bone health may require a broader discussion of a woman's physical and emotional health.“Women need a complete evaluation not a consultation for the issues related to menstruation,” said Dr Priyanka Sharma, senior consultant, obstetrics and gynaecology, Cocoon Hospital, Chandigarh.Barriers such as the cost of travel, time away from work, lack of awareness and limited access to healthcare facilities can make seeking care more difficult. Strengthening primary-level assessment, training healthcare workers and establishing referral pathways could help women receive appropriate support.Education in local languages and more affordable treatment options are also important to ensure that women can understand their symptoms, discuss available choices and access care when needed.Making menopause a routine part of women's healthcare could help shift the focus from simply enduring symptoms to identifying and managing them appropriately.Medical care is only part of the picture. Family attitudes and social expectations can influence whether women feel comfortable discussing menopause or seeking help.“In many Indian households, menopause is still not discussed openly because of social stigma, lack of awareness, and the belief that it is simply a natural process. As a result, many women suffer silently rather than seeking medical help,” said Dr Bharti Soy.When symptoms such as disturbed sleep, irritability or discomfort are dismissed as inevitable consequences of growing older, women may begin to question whether their concerns deserve medical attention.“If relatives tell her that discomfort, irritability or sleep problems are simply part of growing older, she may question whether her concerns deserve medical attention,” said Dr Swati Sinha, senior consultant, obstetrics and gynaecology, Rosewalk by Rainbow Hospitals.Families can help by making menopause a subject that can be discussed without embarrassment or judgement. Listening without dismissing symptoms, offering practical support and encouraging medical consultations when problems affect daily life can make the transition easier to navigate.Partners, children and other family members need not have all the answers. Understanding that menopause affects women differently, and that help is available when symptoms become disruptive, is an important first step.Menopause may be a natural stage of life, but that does not mean women should have to endure its more difficult symptoms without support. Better awareness, informed medical consultations, accessible treatment and understanding families can help ensure that women are heard and their concerns taken seriously.
Article Summary: Menopause can bring a range of physical, emotional and urogenital symptoms. Treatment options for menopause range from hormone therapy and non-hormonal medicines to lifestyle changes. Despite growing conversations around women's health, gaps in awareness, medical guidance and access to appropriate treatment continue to shape their experiences.

NEW DELHI: The Centre has directed social media giant Meta, which owns Instagram and Facebook, to ensure that its recommendation algorithms do not result in "disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives. ""Ensure that recommendation systems do not result in disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives, and endeavour to provide appropriate diversity of relevant and credible information," an advisory issued by the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY), dated October 10, stated, PTI reported."Also strengthen mechanisms for rapid identification, review and escalation of content, which is gaining significant reach through recommendation systems and has the potential to cause widespread public confusion, apprehension, violence or disturbance of public order," it added.While the advisory does not cite any specific incident that led to its issuance, it comes amid ongoing protests in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.MeitY also asked Meta to cooperate with law enforcement and other authorised government agencies by providing information or assistance within the timelines prescribed under the IT Rules, 2021.The ministry noted that certain content relating to "ongoing public events" was being "prominently displayed and recommended to users" on Meta platforms.Citing the Information Technology Act, 2000, the advisory highlighted the company’s obligation to exercise due diligence under the IT Rules, 2021, which require intermediaries to inform users about prohibited content, including material likely to cause public disorder or incite a cognisable offence.MeitY also flagged content presenting old or selectively edited visuals as current events, misleading claims about emergencies, restrictions or police action, and audio-visual material depicting law-and-order situations without adequate context. It also raised concerns over content likely to incite violence and misleading material receiving disproportionate amplification.The advisory outlined six requirements for Meta, including measures to identify and address prohibited content and review recommendation and ranking systems to ensure misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material is not "disproportionately amplified or repeatedly recommended to users".MeitY emphasised that the advisory seeks to promote responsible information dissemination while respecting lawful expression and public discourse."Meta is advised to ensure that any action taken pursuant to this advisory is consistent with the Information Technology Act, 2000, the IT Rules, 2021, and other applicable laws," the ministry added.
Article Summary: The Centre has directed social media giant Meta to ensure that its recommendation algorithms do not result in "disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives" It comes amid ongoing protests in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

Article Title: Phone on speaker in train? You may be penalised, jailed
Article Text:
As per law, creating a nuisance in Metro rail also attracts a penalty and such persons can be removed from coaches (AI image)

NEW DELHI: In a move that could bring relief to railway passengers disturbed by people playing music or watching videos on their phones in speaker mode and check the growing menace, Southern Railway has warned that such behaviour could attract a penalty of Rs 1,000 and lead to removal from railway premises, including coaches. People persisting with such an act could even face up to six months of jail and up to Rs 5,000 penalty.Southern Railway has invoked Section 142 of the Railways Act, as amended under the Jan Vishwas Act, to enforce provisions dealing with causing a nuisance.Officials said that the provision can be invoked by other railway zones and even by Metro systems to check such behaviour, which adversely affects the comfort of other passengers. As per law, creating a nuisance in Metro rail also attracts a penalty and such persons can be removed from coaches.Section 270 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) defines public nuisance as an act that causes common injury, danger, obstruction or annoyance to people using a public right and hence amounts to an offence.In a circular issued to all its divisions this month and marked to Railway Board, Southern Railway flagged the problem of passengers playing music or audio through speakers at railway stations and inside trains, describing it as a “nuisance”.The circular also referred to a Railway Board communication issued in July 2012 on the use of mobile phones. The board had flagged issues such as “loud talking, lengthy conversations” and sound of objectionable ringtones inside coaches and asked all zones to create awareness against such practices.Official communication from Southern Zone stated, “In recent times, with the advent of widespread mobile internet access, the playing of videos and other content in speaker mode is highly prevalent in public spaces. ln the present scenario, there is urgent need to put in place arrangements in order to ensure that travelling passengers are not inconvenienced.”It has directed its divisions to educate passengers on the relevant legal provisions and discourage them from playing music or videos in speaker mode or engaging in loud conversations while travelling or on railway premises. Awareness campaigns are to be conducted through public address systems in regional languages, Hindi and English. It has said that ticket examiners and other senior officials from commercial division can impose the Rs 1,000 penalty on offenders.
Article Summary: Southern Railway has invoked Section 142 of the Railways Act to enforce provisions dealing with causing a nuisance. People persisting with such an act could even face up to six months of jail and up to Rs 5,000 penalty. As per law, creating a nuisance in Metro rail also attracts a penalty.

Article Title: Global uranium production to dip by 50% by 2040 as demand set to double, says IAEA report; forecast could pinch India too
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Global uranium supply constraints would witness mining production drop by at least 50% by 2040 even as demand is set to double, according to the latest International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) report. This IAEA forecast on global uranium supply crunch is likely to affect India’s goal to increase its nuclear capacity to 100 GW by 2047.According to publication ‘Uranium 2024: Resources, Production and Demand’, also known as the ‘Red Book’, jointly prepared by Nuclear Energy Agency of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development and the Agency, global uranium requirements are projected to increase to 90,045 tonnes of uranium (tU) in the low-case scenario and up to 1,42,631 tU in the high-case scenario by 2050, which represents a 50% to 144% increase from today’s requirements of approximately 60,000 tU.In contrast to future doubling of uranium requirements, uranium production from existing mines is forecast to decrease by at least 50% by 2040, the report said. “Conversion capacity is already insufficient and is projected to fall further behind demand through 2040, highlighting the need for substantial new investment and facility expansions. While global enrichment capacity currently exceeds demand, it remains unevenly distributed geographically,” it said.The report suggested new mines and expansion or life extension of existing mines, as well as reopening of idled mines, saying these steps will be required for assurance of supply in the future.Amid the gloomy scenario predicted by IAEA, India has initiated steps to increase nuclear power capacity from current 8,180 MW to 22,480 MW by 2031-32. The expansion includes construction and commissioning of 10 reactors, totalling 8,000 MW, across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Haryana, Karnataka, and MP. Additionally, pre-project activities for 10 more reactors have commenced, with plans for progressive completion by 2031-32. Further, the Modi govt accorded in-principle approval to set up 6 x 1208 MW nuclear power plant in cooperation with the USA at Kovvada in Srikakulam district in Andhra Pradesh.India procures uranium from a combination of domestic mining and international suppliers: Domestic uranium is mined by Uranium Corporation of India Limited (UCIL) from deposits in Jharkhand, Andhra and Karnataka. It relies primarily on natural uranium for its pressurised heavy water reactors and is gradually shifting toward a closed fuel cycle using plutonium-fuelled fast breeder reactors (FBRs) and eventually thorium. To supplement limited domestic reserves and back its expansion targets under HANTI Act, 2025, India imports and has active supply arrangements with Kazakhstan, Russia, Canada, Australia (finalised arrangements under a nuclear cooperation deal), Uzbekistan and France. However, the IAEA prediction of uranium shortfall if drastic steps not taken could pinch India too.Over the next decade, nuclear fuel production will face increasing demand across all nuclear fuel-related segments due to increasing construction programmes in both established and embarking countries, necessitating the development of new fuel types, including for small modular reactors and advanced reactors, it said.“An increase in uranium production will require sustained investment with positive market conditions, and the discovery of new deposits will require sustained long-term exploration efforts, bearing in mind that the development of new uranium mines takes 10–15 years on average, from deposit discovery to the start of mining operations,” it said.In addition, significant and timely investment in exploration and mining/processing technology will be required, including cost-effective uranium extraction techniques for exploiting unconventional deposit types (for example uranium from phosphate and black shale deposits), some of which may become economic if there is a sustained increase in market prices, it suggested.
Article Summary: Global uranium supply constraints would witness mining production drop by at least 50% by 2040. This IAEA forecast on global uranium supply crunch is likely to affect India’s goal to increase its nuclear capacity to 100 GW by 2047. The report suggested new mines and expansion or life extension of existing mines.

Article Title: CISF to reorganise eight territorial sectors into specialised functional units from November 1
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Come November 1, the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) will transition from a region-specific administrative and operational control structure to a purely functional one, ensuring that each of its reorganised sectors caters to the specialised requirements of the industries and establishments secured by it.CISF officials said 8 its 11 territorial sectors spread across the country will be reorganised into functional sectors dedicated to govt installations and museums in Delhi, coal industries, power plants, petroleum and natural gas units, and steel industry etc.The National Capital Region (NCR) region, New Delhi will thus become the Govt Buildings, Museums & Monuments and Mass Rapid Transit System (GBMM & MRTS) sector, New Delhi. The North sector, New Delhi will be reorganised as Power-I sector, Delhi and the North Eastern-II sector, Kolkata as Power-II sector, Kolkata. The Eastern sector, Ranchi will be rechristened as Coal Sector, Ranchi and cater to the security needs of the coalfields guarded by CISF.Similarly, the Central sector will become the dedicated Steel sector based at Bhilai. The North Eastern sector at Guwahati has been transformed into the Petroleum and Natural Gas sector, Guwahati.To fortify India's maritime trade infrastructure, the Western Sector (Mumbai) and South Sector (Chennai) have been respectively transformed into the West Coast Port Sector and the East Coast Port Sector.The existing Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space sector headquartered at Bengaluru as well as the Airport-I sector, New Delhi and Airport-II sector, Bengaluru, will continue under their respective functional arrangements.“The revised structure, approved by CISF DG Praveer Ranjan with the concurrence of ministry of home affairs (MHA), will come into effect from Nov 1, 2026, a CISF spokesperson said on Sunday. Apart from aligning the supervisory structure of the force more closely with the specific security requirements of different sectors, the new arrangement aims to improve operational oversight, promote sector-specific expertise, ensure greater uniformity insecurity practices and strengthen coordination with the concerned ministries, departments and installation managements.Over the past 25 years, CISF has progressively adopted a functional approach in selected sectors, including aviation.The experience gained from this approach has highlighted the advantages of specialised supervision, focused training, sector-specific standard operating procedures (SOPs), better utilisation of specialised personnel and closer coordination with the concerned organisations.
Article Summary: The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) will transition from a region- specific administrative and operational control structure to a purely functional one. 8 of the force's 11 territorial sectors will be reorganised into functional sectors dedicated to govt installations and museums in Delhi, coal industries, power plants, petroleum and natural gas units, and steel industry etc.

Social and cultural-humanitarian cooperation is also expected to feature in the discussions.India has highlighted the need to expand intra-SCO trade, lower trade costs, strengthen supply chains and improve connectivity.At a meeting of SCO ministers responsible for foreign economic and trade activities in Dushanbe in September, India called for simplified customs procedures, paperless trade, electronic document exchange and stronger multimodal connectivity, according to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.India also highlighted opportunities for cooperation in agriculture, critical minerals, pharmaceuticals, manufacturing, electronics, energy security, renewable energy and green hydrogen. It called for greater use of digital and cross-border payments and improved access to trade finance for micro, small and medium enterprises and start-ups.The October meeting will provide India an opportunity to exchange views with other SCO member states on advancing practical and mutually beneficial cooperation. India remains actively engaged in SCO mechanisms and contributes to regional cooperation through initiatives in start-ups and innovation, digital public infrastructure and people-to-people exchanges, the Ministry of Defence said.The Council of Heads of Government adopts the SCO’s budget and addresses key issues related to cooperation within the organisation, particularly in the economic sphere. The body meets annually and is distinct from the Council of Heads of State, which serves as the organisation’s highest decision-making forum.The previous meeting of the Council of Heads of Government was held in Moscow on November 18, 2025, where India was represented by external affairs minister S Jaishankar, according to ANI.
Article Summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will visit Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 19 and 20. He will represent India at the 25th meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s (SCO) Council of Heads of Government. The meeting will focus on strengthening multilateral cooperation.

Article Title: AI cuts job demand in exposed occupations by nearly 10% across Asia: IMF report
Article Text:
As Job Placements Near, India Inc Taps Old IITs for AI Roles

AI creates demand for new skills

India faces jobs and skills challenge

Education, reskilling key to managing AI disruption

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping labour demand across Asia, with employer demand falling by nearly 10% in occupations more exposed to the technology since the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022, according to the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) October 2026 Regional Economic Outlook: Asia and Pacific.The report, based on approximately 40 million online job postings across 19 Asian economies, highlights the challenges facing countries such as India, Indonesia and the Philippines as they seek to create productive jobs for growing working-age populations while AI transforms the sectors expected to absorb new workers.However, the decline in demand for workers in AI-exposed occupations appears to have stabilised, suggesting that the technology’s impact on employment is not limited to job displacement.The IMF report points to the emergence of new employment opportunities requiring specialised AI skills, including prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation and AI agent development.Employers are increasingly seeking workers who can integrate AI into business processes, improve productivity and translate technological capabilities into practical applications.Firm-level adoption of AI, however, remains uneven. Around 6% of firms in Asia explicitly seek AI skills in their job postings, the report said.Businesses adopting AI are experiencing stronger labour demand growth than those that have not adopted the technology, including in occupations highly exposed to automation. This suggests that AI can complement human capabilities even as it reduces demand for certain tasks.The implications of AI differ across Asian economies. Emerging economies such as India may initially be less exposed to the technology because a large share of their workforce remains employed in agriculture and other sectors less affected by AI.However, this could pose a longer-term challenge if AI makes it harder for workers to transition into higher-productivity manufacturing and services, the report said.For countries with expanding working-age populations, the challenge is to generate enough productive employment while ensuring that workers have the skills required by an increasingly technology-driven economy.The report emphasises that the response to AI must go beyond encouraging technological adoption. Education reform, reskilling programmes, digital infrastructure and stronger labour-market institutions will be essential to prepare workers for changing occupational demands.Businesses will also need to invest in workforce development alongside AI adoption to help employees adapt to new roles and changing skill requirements.The report suggests that AI need not become a barrier to inclusive growth. With timely investments in skills and preparedness, Asian economies could use the technology to boost productivity, encourage innovation and support sustainable employment.
Article Summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping labour demand across Asia. Employer demand has fallen by nearly 10% in occupations more exposed to the technology since the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022. The IMF report points to the emergence of new employment opportunities requiring specialised AI skills.

Article Title: FSSAI may curb sugar in baby food, set pesticide caps for tea
Article Text:
The draft amendments were published in the Gazette of India on Oct 16 (AI image)

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has proposed two changes to food safety rules: prohibiting the addition of sucrose and fructose to products meant for babies up to six months and setting maximum residue limits for two pesticides in tea.The draft amendments were published in the Gazette of India on Oct 16. Currently, lactose and glucose polymers are the preferred carbohydrate sources in infant foods. Sucrose and fructose can be added when needed, but their combined amount cannot exceed 20% of total carbohydrates. The proposed amendment seeks to prohibit their addition in products for babies up to six months.The proposal aims to limit early exposure to added sugars amid concerns over childhood obesity and related health risks. It also complements recommendations for exclusive breastfeeding during the first six months. A doctor said the restriction must be enforced at the licensing stage. “FSSAI should also consider extending the ban to products intended for children above six months, given concerns over obesity.FSSAI has also proposed maximum residue limits of 20 parts per million (ppm) for acetamiprid and 50 ppm for imidacloprid in tea.Maxim­um residue limits specify the highest legally permitted co­n­­centration of pesticide residues in food and provide ben­chmarks. They do not indicate the amount necessarily pr­esent in a particular sample.One doctor said the proposed limits need to be accompanied by realistic assessments of consumer exposure. “Since tea is consumed several times a day, it is important to assess how much of these chemicals passes from the leaves into the brewed drink.”
Article Summary: The draft amendments were published in the Gazette of India on Oct 16. Currently, lactose and glucose polymers are the preferred carbohydrate sources in infant foods. The proposed amendment seeks to prohibit their addition in products for babies up to six months. The proposal aims to limit early exposure to added sugars amid concerns over childhood obesity.

Article Title: FSSAI cracks down on Priyagold biscuit maker

The FSSAI has taken legal action against three companies over serious violations of food safety standards

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has stepped up enforcement against major food companies, sanctioning prosecution against Priyagold biscuit maker Surya Food & Agro Ltd, Dodla Dairy Ltd and Ueir Organic Foods Pvt Ltd, while issuing notices to Nestlé India and Hindustan Unilever (HUL) over alleged labelling violations and misleading product claims.Action against Surya Food & Agro followed a consumer complaint that led officials to find bran meant for cattle feed being used as a fibre source in Priyagold biscuits.The gunny bags containing the material for the biscuits were marked for cattle feed. Inspectors also flagged deficiencies in plant hygiene, pest control, raw material storage and segregation, personnel hygiene and premises maintenance. The company’s FSSAI licence was suspended following the inspection, and the competent authority has now sanctioned prosecution. Attempts to reach the company for comment were unsuccessful.FSSAI has issued notices to Nestlé India over its Nescafé ready-to-drink range, including Cappuccino, Choco Mocha and Chilled Latte, manufactured by Schreiber Dynamix Dairies and Lotus Dairy Products. The regulator flagged discrepancies between the front-of-pack description “Flavoured Milk” and the back label, which classified the products as “Proprietary Food – 1.12 Dairy Based Drink”.Online listings described them as “Coffee Flavoured Milk” and carried claims about the goodness of flavoured double-toned milk, which FSSAI said were inconsistent with the declared product category. The companies have been asked to explain why action should not be initiated under food safety laws.A separate notice to Nestlé concerned its Resource Renal vanilla flavour powder, intended for dietary management of people with conservatively treated chronic kidney disease. FSSAI said the product lacked the required prior approval and that the prescribed vegetarian or non-vegetarian symbol was missing from the label.In a statement the company said, “FSSAI has sent a communication to Nestlé India concerning the label declarations/classification of the Nescafe Ready To Drink products. This does not relate to product safety or product quality. Mentioned products are safe to consume and meet all applicable food safety requirements.We will be submitting our response to the authorities and will be engaging with them as per due process established under law. ” Hindustan Unilever was issued notices over claims on Horlicks Women’s Plus Chocolate Nutrition Drink, including “Nutrition for Strong Bones” and “Clinically Proven to Help Improve Bone Strength in 6 Months”.In a statement to the press, the company spokesperson said, “Hindustan Unilever Limited is committed to providing safe, high-quality products that comply with all applicable regulatory requirements. Horlicks Women’s Plus and Mother’s Plus has been developed based on established nutritional science and is manufactured in accordance with stringent quality and safety standards. All product communication is developed in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, and governance processes. We will share all the scientific and regulatory evidence with the authorities as per normal process of review.”
Article Summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has stepped up enforcement against major food companies. The regulator has sanctioned prosecution against Priyagold biscuit maker Surya Food & Agro Ltd, Dodla Dairy Ltd and Ueir Organic Foods Pvt Ltd. It has also issued notices to Nestlé India and Hindustan Unilever over alleged labelling violations and misleading product claims.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million mansion faces new developments as officials schedule another property review
Article Text:
Travis Kelce mansion (Getty Images)

Travis Kelce’s Ohio mansion draws attention over privacy plans

Travis Kelce’s landscaping proposal faces fresh questions

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion offers the privacy and luxury expected of an NFL star, but making the estate more secluded has proved complicated. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end now faces questions from local residents about landscaping, aging sewer lines and the impact of new barriers on the neighborhood. What began as an effort to improve the property has turned into a wider discussion about balancing personal space with community concerns. With another review scheduled for November, Kelce’s plans for his historic lakeside home remain partly unresolved, despite progress on one major renovation proposal.Kelce purchased the 3.5-acre Bratenahl estate on March 2, 2026, for $5.35 million. Located along Lake Erie near Cleveland, the property stands out for its scale, history and impressive facilities.Known as Moyenage, the mansion dates back to 1904. The historic residence spans 21,140 square feet and features eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms, seven fireplaces, a sauna, a fitness centre and a heated outdoor pool. Its grounds also include a five-car garage and a guest cottage created from a former gatehouse.However, improving security around such a large property comes with challenges. Kelce’s proposed fencing initially included an eight-foot barrier, prompting concerns from nearby homeowners about lake views and the appearance of the neighborhood.The revised design received unanimous approval from Bratenahl’s Architectural Review Board on September 8. The plan calls for a six-foot black aluminium fence covering approximately 1,190 linear feet, with matching gates and a design intended to complement existing stone walls.Contractor Jacob Kutz explained that the changes addressed residents’ objections, including concerns about preserving views of Lake Erie. The fence will also sit about two feet inside the property boundary to avoid interfering with shared sewer infrastructure.Although the fence has received approval, the mansion’s landscaping plans have encountered further delays. During an October 6 meeting, village officials examined a proposal to plant evergreen trees behind the property.Residents raised concerns about the trees’ eventual height and their possible impact on neighboring homes. Officials indicated that plants growing below 10 feet could offer privacy without creating the same problems. The board approved the front-yard landscaping but postponed its decision on the rear section.Shared utilities have also become a point of contention. Neighbor Katherine Bolton warned that roots from roughly 50 proposed evergreens could damage an aging sewer line reportedly shared with the estate. She said protecting her section of the pipe could cost $75,000.Kelce’s representatives have discussed a $7,500 repair to part of the shared sewer, and the fence design includes access gates for maintenance crews.Bratenahl’s Architectural Review Board plans to reconsider the landscaping proposal on November 10, 2026. Until then, Kelce’s efforts to improve privacy at Moyenage remain subject to local review and the concerns of those living nearby.
Article Summary: Kelce purchased the 3.5-acre Bratenahl estate on March 2, 2026, for $5.35 million. Known as Moyenage, the mansion dates back to 1904. It features eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms, seven fireplaces, a sauna, a fitness centre and a heated outdoor pool.

Article Title: Sara Blakely was selling fax machines door to door when she put $5,000 of her savings into Spanx; 21 years later, Blackstone bought a majority stake in the company at a $1.2 billion valuation
Article Text:
Despite having no formal business education, Blakely developed her first product from her apartment (Picture: Spanx)

How Sara Blakely started with $5,000

Blackstone's major investment

Oprah Winfrey and Reese Witherspoon join

What changed for Spanx after investment?

In 2000, Sara Blakely was working as a door-to-door fax machine salesperson when she decided to start her own business with $5,000 from her savings. Her idea was to develop a new type of women's undergarment that would offer greater comfort and support. However, she had no formal business training, had never attended a business class and had no outside investors. Nonetheless, she went on to establish Spanx, a company that would eventually become a major name in women's clothing.Twenty-one years later, in October 2021, global investment firm Blackstone announced an agreement to acquire a majority stake in the company at a valuation of $1.2 billion. The deal marked a major change for a business that Blakely had built without raising outside investment.According to Blackstone, Blakely would retain a significant ownership stake and continue working with the company's existing management team. She would also become Executive Chairwoman of Spanx.Alongside Blackstone, several prominent women, including Oprah Winfrey, Reese Witherspoon and Whitney Wolfe Herd, joined as investors. Their involvement brought together businesswomen who had previously supported the company or established successful companies of their own.Blakely's journey began while she was still selling fax machines door to door. She wanted to enter the women's shapewear and undergarment market, an industry that was male-dominated at the time.Despite having no formal business education, she worked on developing her first product from her apartment. She also wrote her own patent application for the undergarment she had invented.The company initially focused on shapewear, a category of clothing designed to provide support and create a smoother appearance under other garments. Over time, it expanded beyond original undergarments into several other clothing categories.Its product range eventually included leggings, denim, trousers, activewear, swimwear and intimate apparel. The company also introduced collections such as Perfect Pants, extending its business into everyday clothing.Blakely was also included in TIME magazine's list of the world's 100 most influential people and appeared on the cover of Forbes as the youngest self-made female billionaire.On October 20, 2021, Blackstone announced that funds managed by the investment firm had agreed to acquire a majority stake in Spanx. The agreement valued the entire company at $1.2 billion, although the exact amount Blackstone paid for its stake was not disclosed.Blakely welcomed the agreement while reflecting on how the company had started. “This is a really important moment in time for female entrepreneurs,” she had said.“I started this company with no business experience and very little money, but I cared the most about the customer, and that gave me the courage to launch the company,” she added,The transaction was formally completed on November 18, 2021, when Spanx and Blackstone announced the participation of several additional investors.Among them were television personality and entrepreneur Oprah Winfrey, actress and Hello Sunshine founder Reese Witherspoon, and Bumble founder Whitney Wolfe Herd. Two female-founded investment firms, G9 Ventures and Able Partners, also participated.Winfrey had played a role in bringing the company to public attention during its early years. In 2000, she included the product in her well-known Favorite Thingsselection.Recalling her first experience with the product, Winfrey said, “When Sara first came on The Oprah Show to tell us about her idea for Spanx, I knew it was brilliant.”She added that the company had become a regular part of her wardrobe and expressed support for the company's continued development.Blakely also described the participation of Winfrey and Witherspoon as particularly meaningful because both had supported the brand for years.Under the agreement, Blakely retained a significant equity stake in Spanx and became its Executive Chairwoman. The existing senior management team also remained involved in overseeing daily operations.Blackstone and Spanx announced plans to establish an all-female board of directors. The Blackstone investment team responsible for the transaction was also made up entirely of women. The transaction also formed part of Blackstone's investments in female-founded businesses.Beyond her business career, Blakely is also committed to philanthropy. In 2013, she signed the Giving Pledge, promising to donate half her wealth to charitable causes. Through her personal foundation, she has already contributed millions of dollars towards supporting women.
Article Summary: Sara Blakely was working as a door-to-door fax machine salesperson when she decided to start her own business with $5,000 from her savings. Her idea was to develop a new type of women's undergarment that would offer greater comfort and support. In October 2021, global investment firm Blackstone announced an agreement to acquire a majority stake in the company at a valuation of $1.2 billion. Oprah Winfrey and Reese Witherspoon joined as investors.

Article Title: In 1968, Cassandra Henderson graduated from a North Carolina school; nearly 60 years later, she moved back into the same building after it was restored from 20 years of vacancy into 53 senior apartmen
Article Text:
Dillard School Senior ApartmentsPhoto credit: https://www.taxcreditcoalition.org/

A school with deep local meaning

From empty building to senior housing

Designed for ageing in place

Why adaptive reuse is important

A homecoming with a larger lesson

Cassandra Henderson graduated from Dillard Junior High in Yanceyville, North Carolina, in 1968. Nearly six decades later, she moved back into the same building, not as a student but as a resident of the newly restored Dillard School Senior Apartments. The former school, which had stood empty for about 20 years, has been transformed into 53 affordable apartments for seniors aged 62 and older, reported Tax Credit Coalition.The project is a rare example of a community turning a vacant historic building into practical housing. Originally built between 1949 and 1951, the Caswell County Training School was the first African American school in Caswell County to offer 11 grades. After desegregation in 1969, it was renamed for longtime principal Nicholas Longworth Dillard and continued serving students until it closed in 2002. Read more details about it here, as per Tax Credit Coalition's report:For generations of Black students in Caswell County, the school was more than a place to learn. It represented opportunity at a time when educational access was shaped by segregation. Its early name, Caswell County Training School, reflected the era’s segregated school system, but the institution became a centre of learning, pride and community life.The campus included a gymnasium addition in 1960, giving students space for athletics and gatherings beyond the classroom. Henderson’s graduation in 1968 came near the end of that era, just before desegregation changed the school’s role and identity.After desegregation, the school was renamed Dillard Junior High in honour of Nicholas Longworth Dillard, its longtime principal. The building continued to serve local students until its closure in 2002, after which it entered a long period of vacancy, as per the report.For two decades, the former school sat unused. Its future was uncertain until community-led preservation efforts helped secure its place on the National Register of Historic Places and build support for a new purpose.The restoration converted former classrooms into seven studio apartments and 46 one-bedroom apartments. All 53 units are restricted to seniors with incomes at or below 50 percent of the area median income, making the development an important affordable-housing option in rural Yanceyville. The project was developed through the work of DreamKey Partners and Red Stone Equity Partners. It also received recognition from the Affordable Housing Tax Credit Coalition, which awarded Dillard School Senior Apartments its 2026 Recognition of Housing Tax Credit Excellence in the Rural Housing category.The apartments were designed to be more than simply affordable. The building includes elevator-served accessibility, a community centre with a business and computer room, fitness space, community laundry, tenant storage and on-site management with supportive service coordination, it was further reported.Outdoor amenities were also built into the plan. Residents have access to community gardens and recreation areas, including pickleball and shuffleboard courts, encouraging neighbours to stay active and connected.For Henderson, returning to the building meant rejoining a place filled with personal history. For other residents it provides a stable home in a familiar community with services and shared spaces designed for later life.The Dillard School project is an example of how historic preservation and affordable housing can go hand in hand. Rather than demolish a prominent local feature, the community preserved its structure and repurposed it to fulfilll a present-day need.Many rural areas face particular housing problems such as little new building, an aging population and a limited choice of rented accommodation. Converting an existing school building into senior apartments can preserve local character while creating homes close to the people and places residents already know.The project also demonstrates the value of patient, community-led redevelopment. The school’s revival did not happen quickly. It required years of vacancy, preservation advocacy, historic recognition and investment before it could become housing again.Cassandra Henderson’s return gives the Dillard School Senior Apartments a human story at their centre. A building that once shaped her education now provides her with a home, nearly 60 years after she walked its halls as a student.The transformation also offers a broader lesson for towns considering the future of vacant schools, factories and civic buildings. When communities protect historic places and adapt them carefully, they can retain memory while addressing urgent needs such as senior housing.Today, Dillard School Senior Apartments is a preserved landmark and active community. The 53 apartments are more than brick and classrooms returned; they are a new lease on life for a building that continues to serve the people of Yanceyville.
Article Summary: Dillard School in Yanceyville, North Carolina, was the first African American school in Caswell County to offer 11 grades. After desegregation in 1969, it was renamed for longtime principal Nicholas Longworth Dillard. The building continued to serve local students until its closure in 2002, after which it entered a long period of vacancy. The former school, which had stood empty for about 20 years, has been transformed into 53 affordable apartments.

Article Title: Bank holiday this week: When and where will banks remain shut from October 19 to 25? Check state-wise list
Article Text:
Bank holidays this week

When and where will banks remain shut this week?

Monday, October 19

Tuesday, October 20

Wednesday, October 21

Thursday and Friday, October 22 and 23

India has officially entered the festive season, with celebrations lined up one after another. But while the calendar fills up with festivals, bank customers may want to keep an eye on another list: the October bank holidays.Before setting out for a branch visit, it is worth checking whether the bank is open or taking a festive break.Bank holidays in October will vary across cities and states, depending on regional observances and festivals. Customers planning large cash deposits, cheque processing, demand drafts or other branch-dependent work should check the holiday schedule for their particular location and plan accordingly.Banks are closed in Tripura, Mizoram, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Uttarakhand, Assam, Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Kerala, Nagaland, West Bengal, Bihar, and Jharkhand for Dussehra (Mahashtami), Maha Navami, Ayutha Pooja, Durga Puja, Vijaya Dashomi, and Durga Ashtami.Banks are closed in Tripura, Gujarat, Mizoram, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Chandigarh, Tamil Nadu, Uttarakhand, Assam, Telangana, Arunachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jammu and Kashmir, Uttar Pradesh, Kerala, Nagaland, West Bengal, Delhi, Goa, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Himachal Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh for Dasara/Dusshera (Vijaya Dashmi), Maha Navami, Ayudhapooja, and Durga Puja.Banks stay open only in Sikkim and Manipur.Banks are closed in Tripura, Karnataka, Sikkim, Assam, Kerala, West Bengal, and Meghalaya for Vijaya Dasami, Durga Puja (Dasain), and Maha Dashami.Banks are closed in Sikkim for Durga Puja (Dasain).In addition to these holidays, banks across the country will remain closed on October 24, the fourth Saturday of the month. As per the RBI's holiday schedule, all scheduled and non-scheduled banks observe a holiday on the second and fourth Saturdays of every month.The good news is that a closed branch does not mean banking comes to a complete standstill. ATMs, UPI, internet banking and mobile banking apps will remain available for routine transactions such as fund transfers, bill payments and account management.However, services requiring a physical branch visit may have to wait until it reopens.A quick check of the holiday calendar could save customers an unnecessary trip and help keep their banking plans on track amid the festive rush.
Article Summary: Bank holidays in October will vary across cities and states, depending on regional observances and festivals. Customers planning large cash deposits, cheque processing, demand drafts or other branch-dependent work should check the holiday schedule for their particular location. ATMs, UPI, internet banking and mobile banking apps will remain available for routine transactions.
